metadata.title: Initial Findings from the IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report summarizes initial findings from the 2009 IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study (ICCS) across 38 countries, using student and teacher data collected in over 5,300 schools. The excerpt provided does not specify whether complex survey sampling weights and replicate weights were applied in the analyses, nor does it name any weight variables (e.g., student design weights or BRR/jackknife replicate weights). For ICCS secondary analysis, analysts should use the IEA-provided sampling weights and replicate weights from the international database to account for the multistage clustered design (students within schools within countries). Because the excerpt does not document the exact weighting implementation, the safest interpretation is that weighting procedures follow IEA ICCS technical documentation rather than being described in this initial-findings text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document excerpt is a high-level initial findings report describing the ICCS study scope and reporting themes (civic knowledge, attitudes, engagement, and contextual influences), but it does not provide methodological details on plausible values (PVs) or missing-data handling procedures. ICCS includes scaled questionnaire and achievement measures, but the excerpt does not specify whether cognitive achievement scores were PV-based, WLE/theta-based, or how missing responses were treated. Therefore, the missing-data handling is classified as not_reported due to the absence of explicit methodological documentation in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the full available ICCS 2009 study sample for the participating countries as described in the report excerpt (more than 140,000 students in 38 countries; over 5,300 schools). The excerpt does not specify any additional analytic subsampling (e.g., grade restriction, module restriction, or exclusions for incomplete questionnaires), so no further filtering criteria can be extracted from the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 is an IEA large-scale comparative study of civic and citizenship education conducted in 38 countries, collecting data from more than 140,000 students, about 62,000 teachers, and over 5,300 schools. The report excerpt frames the study’s purpose and organization and outlines the initial findings that will be reported in subsequent sections: variations in civic knowledge across countries, changes in civic content knowledge since earlier IEA civic studies, and students’ attitudes and civic engagement (including trust, interest, and participation). It also highlights the roles of schools and communities (e.g., classroom climate and implementation of civic education) and the influence of family background (including immigrant background and parental occupational status). The excerpt does not provide the technical scaling, sampling-weighting, or missing-data procedures, nor does it report model-based performance metrics, so the findings should be interpreted as descriptive comparative results rather than as outputs from an explicitly specified predictive ML pipeline.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an IEA initial-findings report excerpt rather than an empirical ML paper with explicitly specified predictive models, target variables, and performance metrics. The provided text does not include the technical methodology needed to extract PV handling, missing-data treatment, analytic sample filtering, or any ML algorithm evaluation. As a result, the extraction focuses on study scope and reporting themes, while leaving ML-specific fields empty and marking missing methodological details as not_reported/not_applicable.
